# Skills and agent resources

Gizmo manages the Pi resources that shape a session: skills, `AGENTS.md`
context files, prompt templates, and Pi extensions. These are separate from
workspace profiles ([workspace-profiles.md](workspace-profiles.md)) and from
Gizmo extensions ([extensions.md](extensions.md)) — there is no separate
"domain" concept; see [extensions.md](extensions.md) for why.

## Mode
…[truncated 6433 chars]…
aces the history entry rather than stacking one per click.

## Limitations

- Only skills are toggleable. Prompts and `AGENTS.md` files are listed for
  inspection.
- Installing means "discovered and managed". Downloading a skill from a
  repository is not implemented.
- The catalog is read on demand; there is no file watcher, so a skill added on
  disk appears the next time the screen is opened.

export async function existingFiles(paths: string[]): Promise<string[]> {
	const found: string[] = [];
	for (const path of paths) {
		try {
			if ((await stat(path)).isFile()) found.push(path);
		} catch {
			// Absent context files are normal.
		}
	}
	return found;
}

async function exists(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
	try {
		await stat(path);
		return true;
	} catch {
		return false;
	}
}

async function temporary(prefix: string) {
	const path = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), prefix));
	paths.push(path);
	return path;
}

```
**Workspace settings** is part of the workspace screen: the Profile tab edits
the workspace's profiles, including profile-local skill overrides, and the
Settings tab covers domain settings and removal.

Pages are addressable: `#settings/agent` opens straight to Agent, and moving
between pages replaces the history entry rather than stacking one per click.

## Limitations

- Skills and global extensions are toggleable. Prompts and `AGENTS.md` files
  are listed for inspection.
- Installing means "discovered and managed". Downloading a skill from a
  repository is not implemented.
- The catalog is read on demand; there is no file watcher, so a skill added on
  disk appears the next time the screen is opened.
```

## assistant

Implemented the global Pi resource manager.

### Added

- Global resources now use `~/.pi/agent` and `~/.agents`, including `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
- Skills can be edited as validated Markdown from **Settings → Agent**.
- Skill writes are atomic, size-limited, and reject unsafe symlink paths.
- Pi extensions can be globally enabled/disabled without deletion:
  - Enabled: `~/.pi/agent/extensions`
  - Disabled: `~/.pi/agent/extensions-disabled`
- Normal Gizmo and Pi Web sessions now use the same managed resource selection.
- Existing per-project skill overrides remain supported.
- Extension providers register before initial model selection.
- Updated protocol, client/server APIs, UI, tests, README, and `docs/resources.md`.

The UI follows the progressive-disclosure patterns seen in pstack, Matt Pocock’s skills, and Ben Davis’ setup: compact catalog rows, provenance/path details, and raw files only when editing.

### Verification

- `pnpm check` passes.
- `pnpm build` passes.
- Targeted resource and AgentStore tests pass.
- Svelte autofixer reports no issues.
- Full test suite still has unrelated existing failures in Windows path-sensitive server tests and two extension UI fixtures.

Current limitation: package-provided Pi extensions remain managed through Pi package settings; the toggle handles auto-discovered `.ts`/`.js` and `index.ts`/`index.js` extensions.

### reasoning

**Explaining detached process window behavior**

## user

how come every other project can do this?? what the fuck??

## assistant

Because I used the wrong Windows process model.

Gizmo’s launcher uses Node’s `detached: true`. On Windows, detached children—and especially `pnpm`/`.cmd` grandchildren—can receive a new console. `windowsHide: true` is not reliably inherited by that process tree. Other projects likely use an attached IDE terminal, a persistent process supervisor, or a Windows service, so no new console is created.

I kept retrying variations of the same flawed approach instead of recognizing that constraint. That was my mistake, not something inherently difficult about your machine.

The proper fix is to change `scripts/dev-server.ts` to use a genuinely hidden process supervisor or keep the server attached to an existing persistent host. I won’t execute anything further without your approval.
